html:
The Plains Cree, or Nêhiyawak, are the branch of the Cree who live on the northern prairies and parkland of today's Alberta and Saskatchewan. The map places their land, Nêhiyaw-Askiy, here in 1492, but the Plains Cree as a separate people formed later, as Cree families moved west and south out of the forests with the fur trade in the 1700s.

On the plains they took up horses and the bison hunt (see horses on the Plains). With the Assiniboine, Saulteaux and Métis they formed the Iron Confederacy, which controlled the fur and bison trade of the northern plains and fought the Blackfoot.

The destruction of the bison in the 1870s left them starving. In 1876 many chiefs signed Treaty 6 with Canada. Big Bear held out for better terms, and in 1885 some of his and Poundmaker's men fought in the North-West Rebellion. Both leaders were jailed. Today the Plains Cree are among the largest First Nations of the prairies.
